Should your product catalogue be a PDF or web pages?

A hypothetical Varanasi packaging supplier follows one wholesale enquiry to decide how to split its catalogue between web pages and a PDF.

By SiteSutra · 27 November 2026

← All articlesYour next step ↓

Put the details customers need to choose a product or request a quote on web pages. Keep a PDF when buyers need one file to forward, print or use offline. If you use both, decide which version your team updates first and tell customers where to confirm details that change.

The buyer needs one carton size

Imagine Farah runs a hypothetical packaging supplier in Varanasi. A mithai shop is preparing festival orders and wants to know whether a carton will fit its existing sweet box. Farah sends the full catalogue. On a phone, the buyer has to zoom into several pages to find the internal dimensions, then retype the carton code in a message. The catalogue is useful to the purchasing team later, when it needs a file to circulate. Farah’s immediate problem is helping someone identify one carton and ask about it.

She tries a page for the carton family with common sizes, units, product codes and a quote link. She keeps the PDF for the purchasing team. Before adding pages for the rest of the range, she decides what information belongs in each format.

Give each detail a home

Farah’s plan for the carton range
What the buyer needsWhere it belongsWhat to verify
Find a carton that fitsWeb page with dimensions and product codesState whether dimensions are internal or external and use consistent units
Forward the range for reviewDated PDF with a link to the current catalogueMake the edition visible in the file so a forwarded copy keeps its date
Confirm availability for a deadlineQuote request with the product code and requested delivery dateExplain which details the team confirms after receiving the request
Check a drawing or specification sheetProduct page summary with a labelled downloadMatch the document to the product code and revision

Start with one page per product family when buyers compare similar sizes and take the same next step. Give a variant its own page when it needs genuinely different information, such as distinct materials, compatibility or installation requirements. Farah can describe several carton sizes together and give the buyer a code to refer to.

Check how the catalogue reads on a phone

Try finding a product code and reading its dimensions at a larger text size. Use real text for the fields buyers read and copy, and keep the units next to the numbers. A comparison table may need to scroll within its own container. Keep the surrounding page readable without side scrolling. The W3C’s reflow guidance explains the narrow viewport requirement and its exceptions for content that needs a two-dimensional layout. W3C reflow guidance.

Open the PDF on the same phone. Check whether a buyer can search for the product code and find the revision date. Google lists PDF and HTML among the formats it can index. Choose the format based on how your buyer will use it, then check that the file and page both point to the right next step. Google’s indexable file types.

Make one person responsible for the specification

Farah’s team keeps product codes and dimensions in one approved product record. When a specification changes, the owner checks the page and the downloadable edition before marking the update complete. The team treats old PDFs in inboxes as snapshots. Each edition includes the catalogue link so its readers can confirm current details.

For availability and order quantities that staff confirm case by case, the product page explains what the buyer should provide. Farah asks for the carton code, requested quantity and delivery date. She can review the actual received enquiries for completeness. Search impressions and clicks answer a different question about discovery, and AI citations can be recorded independently.

Try one product family before rebuilding the catalogue

Farah asks someone unfamiliar with the range to open one page on a phone, identify a suitable code and prepare a test quote request. She also asks a colleague to forward the PDF and check whether the recipient can find the current edition. She records where either person gets stuck before deciding what to publish next.

If this is part of a redesign, use the redesign URL inventory to track existing catalogue links and the enquiry form test guide to confirm receipt. SiteSutra’s website development service explains how to scope the build.
